hero.badge: An AI trading mentor for beginners
hero.title: Practice trading decisions on real forex charts, without real money
hero.body: TRY-REX is a place for beginners to learn forex trading. Learn the basics through levelled lessons, practice BUY, SELL or WAIT decisions on historical charts with the reasons explained, then practice discipline in a demo account with a virtual balance.
hero.note: The Trading Game and Learn 101 work right away, no sign-up needed.

about.title: A place to practice, not a place to bet
about.body: Most retail traders lose money, and TRY-REX doesn't promise profit. What it trains is how you make decisions: reading the chart, planning before you enter, and keeping risk small.
about.body2: It's built for beginners: the lessons come in order, hard terms can be tapped to see what they mean, and every answer comes with its reasons.

real.title: Real charts, nothing made up
real.body: Trading Game questions, the charts in lessons and the Demo Account chart all use historical forex price data. No price is invented.

virtual.title: Virtual money
virtual.body: The Trading Game and the Demo Account use a virtual balance. There's no deposit, and the balance can't be withdrawn or exchanged.

process.title: Judged on process
process.body: In the Demo Account, every trade is scored on {checks} Disiplin checks: stop loss, risk size, reward ratio, an SL that isn't moved away, and no revenge trading. Profit or loss doesn't change the score.

notBroker.title: Not a broker, not signals
notBroker.body: TRY-REX takes no real orders, gives no signals and never asks you to open a broker account. Everything is educational.

surfaces.title: Six parts, one learning path
surfaces.body: In the order beginners learn: get to know yourself, learn the basics, practice decisions, then put them to work.

start.title: Starting quiz
start.body: A short quiz of {quiz, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}} sets your first question level, the pairs you focus on and your daily practice target. There are no wrong answers.

learn.title: Learn 101
learn.body: {levels, plural, one {# level} other {# levels}} and {lessons, plural, one {# lesson} other {# lessons}}, from forex basics to trading psychology. Each level ends with a {examQuestions}-question exam; pass it to open the next level.

game.title: Trading Game
game.body: {questions, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}} from historical H4 charts of {gamePairs, plural, one {# forex pair} other {# forex pairs}}. Choose BUY, SELL or WAIT, then read the AI Explanation of why.

demo.title: Demo Account
demo.body: Trade a virtual ${balance} balance on {livePairs, plural, one {# pair} other {# pairs}} and {timeframes, plural, one {# timeframe} other {# timeframes}}, on a chart that runs on real time. Opens after {sessions, plural, one {# Trading Game session} other {# Trading Game sessions}}.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.body: Level, XP, streak, practice calendar and daily target. Every number comes from your own practice.

kamus.title: Trading Glossary
kamus.body: {glossary, plural, one {# term} other {# terms}}, each explained in a sentence or two. Underlined terms in questions and lessons can be tapped to see what they mean.

learn.title: Levelled lessons, with an exam at every level
learn.body: The lessons go from basic to advanced. Level 1 is open from the start; each next level opens once you pass the exam of the level before it.

points.1: {lessons, plural, one {# short lesson} other {# short lessons}}, with chart examples from real price data.
points.2: A {examQuestions}-question multiple-choice exam at every level; pass with at least {examPass} right. Questions are shuffled, so every attempt is different.

game.title: Practice decisions on real historical charts
game.body: Each question shows {history} candles and hides the next {future}. You choose, then the chart reveals what actually happened.

points.1: {questions, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}} from {gamePairs, plural, one {# forex pair} other {# forex pairs}}, at Easy, Medium and Hard levels.
points.2: {round, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}} per session, with XP for every right answer.
points.3: What price did next is one sample out of many possibilities, not proof that a decision was certain to be right.

explanation.title: Know why, not just right or wrong
explanation.body: After you answer, the AI Explanation appears right on the same page.

points.1: The trend of the last {history} candles, the nearest support and resistance, and where price sits in its range.
points.2: A suggestion you can use on the next question, including where a stop loss makes sense.
points.3: All of it is computed from that question's own candles, so the explanation always matches the chart.

demo.title: Practice with rules, not gut feeling
demo.body: After {sessions, plural, one {# Trading Game session} other {# Trading Game sessions}}, you can open a demo account with a virtual ${balance} balance.

points.1: The chart runs on real time across {livePairs, plural, one {# pair} other {# pairs}} and {timeframes, plural, one {# timeframe} other {# timeframes}}, with EMA 20, EMA 50, RSI 14 and drawing tools.
points.2: Every order needs a stop loss and a take profit, and the calculator shows the risk before you enter.
points.3: Every trade is scored on {checks} Disiplin checks and recorded in the journal.
points.4: The next stage opens when your discipline is consistent, not when your account is up.

how.title: Learn, practice, then put it to work
how.body: The suggested order. You're free to skip ahead, but each step prepares the next.

s1.title: Learn the basics
s1.body: Read the Learn 101 lessons and pass each level's exam to open the next.

s2.title: Practice decisions
s2.body: Answer Trading Game questions, then read the AI Explanation to see why.

s3.title: Practice with discipline
s3.body: After {sessions, plural, one {# session} other {# sessions}}, open the Demo Account: set SL and TP, keep risk in check, and record every trade in the journal.

s4.title: Track your progress
s4.body: See your level, XP, streak and practice calendar on the Dashboard.

money.a: No. The Trading Game and the Demo Account use a virtual balance and historical price data. There's no deposit, and the balance can't be withdrawn or exchanged.

broker.q: Is TRY-REX a broker or a signal service?
broker.a: No. TRY-REX takes no real orders, gives no trading signals and never asks you to open a broker account. Everything is educational, not financial advice.

data.q: Where does the chart data come from?
data.a: From real historical forex price data. Trading Game questions use H4 candles. The Demo Account replays M15 candles on real time, from a period kept secret so you can't know what happens next.

account.a: Not to start. The Trading Game and Learn 101 work without an account, and your progress is saved on your device. You need an account for the Dashboard and the Demo Account. When you sign up, your Trading Game results on the device move to your account.

demo.q: When does the Demo Account open?
demo.a: After {sessions, plural, one {# Trading Game session} other {# Trading Game sessions}} ({round} questions per session) while signed in. The first time you open it, there's a short lesson to finish first.

scoring.a: In the Trading Game, your answer is compared with how price moved over the next {future} candles, and the AI Explanation explains why. In the Demo Account, the Disiplin score looks only at process: a stop loss at entry, risk at most {maxRisk}% of the balance, reward at least {minRr}× the risk, an SL not moved away, and no revenge trading.

language.a: Indonesian and English. You can switch any time with the ID | EN button, and the Learn 101 lessons are available in both.

cta.title: Start with one question today
cta.body: Free to start. Answer one question, read the explanation, and see what a real chart can teach you.

footer.tagline: A place for beginners to learn forex trading: levelled lessons, questions from real charts, and a demo account with virtual money.
footer.risk: Trading involves risk. Content is educational, not financial advice.
